issues.description: Bookstore.init(books: ...) parameter type mismatch: The problem statement specifies an initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) (an array of Book). The solution implementation declares init(books: Set<Book>) while the stored property in the same solution is declared as let books: [Book]. This mismatch (initializer parameter Set<Book> vs. expected [Book] and vs. stored property type) will confuse students and cause compilation errors because a Set<Book> cannot be directly assigned to a [Book] property without conversion, and students implementing the initializer as specified by the problem will find the solution inconsistent with the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the initializer signature consistent with the problem statement and the stored property. Preferred fix: change the solution initializer to `init(books: [Book]) { self.books = books }`. If a Set is intentionally desired, update the problem statement and the stored property to use `Set<Book>` and ensure `Book` conforms to `Hashable`, or convert the Set to an Array inside the initializer (e.g. `self.books = Array(books)`) but keep the public signature aligned with the documented requirement.

issues.description: Constructor parameter type mismatch for the Bookstore initializer: the problem statement requires an initializer with the signature `init(books: [Book])` (problem_statement.md lines 9-12), but the solution defines `init(books: Set<Book>)` in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift (lines 14-16). The template file (Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift, lines 3-16) is where students are expected to implement the Bookstore, so this inconsistency between the spec and the solution (and with Client.assembleBookstore which supplies a `[Book]`) will confuse students about the expected API and may cause compilation mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the initializer signature consistent with the problem statement and Client usage. Preferable fix: change the solution initializer to `init(books: [Book])` in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift and assign `self.books = books`. Alternatively, if Sets are intended, update the problem statement, template, and Client to use `Set<Book>` consistently — but pick one collection type and apply it across problem statement, template, solution, and Client.
